title: The CANYON course: the commander rides head-out up the ravine into the second choke; the 45 mm gun at the factory edge opens fire; the crewman drops to the gunner's sight and answers
input_audit: The course as the title menu's Canyon entry fields it (the two T-34 platoons on their beats, one 45 mm gun per choke sited by the field-of-fire probe, riflemen in the ruins, one crewman). Disclosed staging: the Tiger stands on the second choke's route at the point its gun sees nearest 430 m (beyond the gun's 400 m opening range), facing up the ravine, its turret laid on the gun's shield, and the gun's crew has heard the fight; the platoons, the other guns and the riflemen keep their own states. The crewman opens the hatch, rides head-out and drives up the ravine from 1.5 s (the gun opens fire once the Tiger is in its range); at 13.5 s he ducks in and moves to the gunner's sight; the disclosed lay_on_at_gun fixture lays the turret on the gun's shield (14.3 s, 21 s) and the disclosed staged_discharge fixture fires twice along that lay (a serviceable round seated). Every mark in the frame comes from the game; every level is the calibration's physical level at the ear through the live Audio graph.
historical_scope: The CANYON playtest course (docs/CANYON_COURSE_20260929.md): a composite of Stalingrad's balkas with a workers' settlement and a factory edge, held by a rifle battalion's 45 mm guns and two T-34 platoons; a playtest course, not a recorded engagement.
